AI Workflows

A sample of my AI work in recruiting.

These examples span the recruiting process, from kickoff through reporting, with one workflow per stage. Each overview highlights the challenge, purpose, and intended benefit.

Intake→Generate→Review→Ship→Learn
01

Interview Guide Generator

Intake and Kickoff

The Problem

Unclear role expectations can lead to misalignment before a search even starts.

What It Does

Helps Recruiters develop interview guidance aligned with the role and hiring priorities.

Quality Check

I check that the guidance reflects the role and confirm alignment with the Hiring Manager.

Designed to Support

A clearer shared understanding of what the team needs to assess.

Interested in this work?

Interested in how AI can help bring clarity to a kickoff? I’d be happy to share my perspective.

02

Role Market Scanner

Recruiting Strategy

The Problem

Hiring expectations can be disconnected from the market, making it harder to agree on a search direction.

What It Does

Organizes research on the talent market to inform recruiting strategy and stakeholder conversations.

Quality Check

I check source quality and relevance and flag uncertainty before sharing findings.

Designed to Support

More informed discussions about role expectations and where to focus the search.

Interested in this work?

Exploring how market context can inform a search? Let’s compare notes.

Let's connect ↗
03

Boolean Search Generator

Sourcing

The Problem

Building a thoughtful search strategy takes time, especially for a complex or unfamiliar role.

What It Does

Helps Recruiters develop Boolean searches for Sales roles.

Quality Check

I review search relevance and consider whether the approach unnecessarily narrows the candidate pool.

Designed to Support

A stronger starting point for sourcing, with room for Recruiter judgment.

Interested in this work?

Working through a sourcing challenge? I’d enjoy hearing how you’re approaching it.

04

Candidate Interview Prep One-Pager

Interview Process

The Problem

Candidates can enter interviews without a clear understanding of what to expect or how to prepare.

What It Does

Creates a concise preparation guide to help candidates understand what to expect in their interviews.

Quality Check

I review accuracy, tone, and alignment with the interview process.

Designed to Support

A more informed candidate experience and more focused interview conversations.

Interested in this work?

Have ideas about better candidate preparation? I’d love to hear them.

05

Offer Strategy Partner

Offer and Closing

The Problem

Offer conversations involve competing priorities and deserve thoughtful preparation.

What It Does

Helps Recruiters prepare for offer discussions and consider negotiation approaches.

Quality Check

Compensation guidance and offer decisions stay with the appropriate people. Sensitive details require care.

Designed to Support

Clearer preparation and more thoughtful communication during closing.

06

Recruiting Status Report

Reporting

The Problem

Turning recruiting updates into a clear stakeholder summary can take time away from the work itself.

What It Does

Helps turn recruiting updates into a concise report for the VP of Sales I support.

Quality Check

I verify facts and figures and review the context before sharing an update.

Designed to Support

Better visibility into hiring progress, priorities, and areas that need attention.

I created a skills repository to bring reusable AI resources into one place, making them easier to find and build on.

My Guardrails

Clear Boundaries

AI never scores, ranks, or rejects candidates. Those decisions stay with a Recruiter or Hiring Manager.

Risk-Graded

I assess each new use case as green, yellow, or red before using it in candidate interactions.

Clean Data

I use only the information a workflow needs. Sensitive details stay out of prompts and public demos.
